scope: Global and secondary senior men's club competitions active in 2026 or 2026-27, beyond the 12 confederation competitions in international.json. Ids are stable dataset codes, NOT Transfermarkt ids.

competitions.name: FIFA Club World Cup
competitions.id_note: stable code, not a Transfermarkt id
competitions.clubs_note: 32 in 2025 (the first edition of the quadrennial format). FIFA has told the confederations the 2029 edition is likely to be larger; 48 is reported but not confirmed.
competitions.participants: Continental champions of the four-year cycle 2021-2024 plus ranked clubs: UEFA 12, CONMEBOL 6, AFC 4, CAF 4, CONCACAF 4, OFC 1, host 1. Maximum two clubs per association, except when more than two clubs from one association won the confederation's top competition.
competitions.qualification: No 2026 edition: the competition is quadrennial (2025, then 2029). Access is by continental title and a four-year club ranking, not by domestic league position. The 2029 access list has not been published.

competitions.quote: UEFA was awarded the most slots with twelve, while CONMEBOL was given the second most with six. The AFC, CAF, and CONCACAF were all given four slots, while the OFC and the host association were given one slot each.
competitions.note: Not playable in a 2026-27 career season: the next edition is 2029. Model it as a once-per-four-seasons competition, not an annual one. Format is World-Cup-like: 8x4 groups, top two, single-leg knockout, no third-place match, no two-legged ties. 2025 ran 14 June - 13 July in the USA (63 matches).

competitions.name: FIFA Intercontinental Cup
competitions.id_note: stable code, not a Transfermarkt id
competitions.clubs_note: 6 clubs, one per confederation. Four matches in total.
competitions.participants: The six reigning confederation club champions. UEFA enters at the final; CONMEBOL and CONCACAF enter the second round; AFC, CAF and OFC enter the first/second round.
competitions.qualification: Continental champions only, no ranking places. In 2026: AFC = 2025-26 AFC Champions League Elite winner, CAF = 2025-26 CAF Champions League winner, CONCACAF = 2026 Champions Cup winner, CONMEBOL = 2026 Copa Libertadores winner, OFC = 2026 OFC Professional League winner, UEFA = 2025-26 UEFA Champions League winner.

competitions.quote: The Recopa Sudamericana was played on a home-and-away two-legged basis, with the Copa Libertadores winners hosting the second leg. If tied on aggregate, 30 minutes of extra time would be played.
competitions.note: A two-legged super cup - the only one in this set besides the CONCACAF finals. Home advantage is fixed by which title the club won, so a super cup model that only knows "neutral venue" cannot express it. Lanús beat Flamengo 4-2 on aggregate.

competitions.name: CONCACAF Central American Cup
competitions.id_note: stable code, not a Transfermarkt id
competitions.participants: Clubs of the seven Central American associations by domestic results: Costa Rica 4, Guatemala 4, El Salvador 3, Honduras 3, Panama 3, Nicaragua 2, Belize 1. Apertura and Clausura champions plus overall-table places.
competitions.qualification: Domestic league places only (no cup route quoted). Slot allocation is fixed per association, not by coefficient.
competitions.league_phase_shape: Four groups of five, single round-robin (4 matches per club, two home and two away). Winners and runners-up (8) to the quarter-finals; the four losing quarter-finalists play a two-legged play-in for the last two Champions Cup places.

berth_links.rule: four semi-finalists plus two play-in winners (6 places); champion to the round of 16, the other five to round one

competitions.quote: The four semi-finalists and the two play-in winners will qualify for the 2027 CONCACAF Champions Cup. The tournament champions will receive a bye to the Champions Cup round of 16, while the remaining five qualified clubs will enter in round one.
competitions.note: Groups of FIVE, not four, and a two-legged final: neither shape exists in the 12 confederation competitions. The play-in is a second-chance bracket that exists only to fill Champions Cup places. Uses the away goals rule (see gaps).

competitions.quote: The winners, Auckland FC, qualified for the 2026 FIFA Intercontinental Cup, with a potential pathway to the 2029 FIFA Club World Cup.
competitions.note: This is why it matters: from 2026 the OFC berth to the Intercontinental Cup and the Club World Cup comes from this league, not from the OFC Men's Champions League ("The 2024 and 2025 editions of the competition featured the winner of the OFC Men's Champions League instead of the OFC Professional League."). The OFC Champions League therefore becomes a domestic-qualification competition with no global berth. It also imports a cross-confederation club (South Melbourne, Australia) into an OFC competition, and Auckland FC is an A-League club.
